subject: toilet flush
title: What If You Always Flushed With the Lid Up?

scenes.text: What if you never closed the toilet lid? Closing it may not help as much as you think.
In 2022, Colorado scientists lit a flushing toilet with green lasers to see what normally stays invisible.
A cloud of tiny droplets shot up at over two meters a second, reaching about five feet within eight seconds.
The smallest droplets can hang in the air for minutes or longer.
Then in 2024, an Arizona team tested lid up against lid down. Virus spread on the toilet and floor came out about the same.
The seat was the dirtiest spot. What actually worked was disinfectant plus a brush, which removed nearly all of it.

description:
What if you always flushed with the lid up? University of Colorado Boulder researchers (Scientific Reports, 2022) used lasers to film a lidless toilet's flush plume: it rose at over 2 m/s and reached about 1.5 m (5 ft) within 8 seconds, and the smallest aerosols can linger for minutes.
A 2024 University of Arizona study (American Journal of Infection Control) found lid up versus lid down made no significant difference to virus contamination on the toilet and floor; disinfectant plus brushing removed over 99.99% from the toilet.
